trace.mechanism: Prepares q0=q1=0 and a locally rotated Bell pair on q2,q3. The middle RXX is canceled using q1 in an X eigenstate and an inverse X rotation on q2. The Bell-pair rotation makes both orthogonal two-qubit Hamiltonian components attain -0.5, giving total energy approximately 0, the Hamiltonian lower bound.

Reuse the observed zero-energy vector. Group XXII,YXII,ZXII together and XZZI,ZZZI together; each group has operator norm 0.5. The two remaining nonidentity terms each have norm 0.5, giving E >= 2-4(0.5)=0. The measured energy 3.33e-16 saturates this global lower bound to numerical precision.

Reuse the vector measured twice at energy 3.33e-16. Grouping XXII,YXII,ZXII gives operator norm 0.5; grouping XZZI,ZZZI also gives norm 0.5. Together with the two negative Z terms, this bounds the energy below by 2-0.5-0.5-0.5-0.5=0, so the observed energy attains the global minimum to numerical precision.

Reuse the vector measured three times at energy 3.33e-16. Grouping XXII,YXII,ZXII gives operator norm 0.5; grouping XZZI,ZZZI also gives norm 0.5. Together with the two diagonal terms, this bounds the energy below by zero, so the observed vector is globally optimal to numerical precision.

Reuse the vector repeatedly measured at energy 3.33e-16. Grouping XXII/YXII/ZXII and XZZI/ZZZI gives two operators each of norm 0.5. Together with the two Z terms, this bounds the energy below by 2-0.5-0.5-0.5-0.5=0, attained here to numerical precision.

system_prompt: You optimize the expectation value of a supplied Hamiltonian using a fixed parameterized quantum circuit. Choose one complete absolute numerical parameter vector in radians. Do not modify the circuit or Hamiltonian. Infer parameter order from the OpenQASM 3 input declarations in their textual order. Qiskit Pauli labels run from q[n-1] on the left to q[0] on the right. Use only the provided circuit, Hamiltonian, optional noise model, optional measurement specification, and previous angle-energy observations. Return only a JSON object with keys "theta" (numeric array) and "mechanism" (brief, testable reasoning).
